title: Self-play tree search designs antimicrobial peptides tested in vitro
summary: A reinforcement learning framework using surrogate-guided self-play Monte Carlo tree search optimised antimicrobial peptides with surrogate activity, HemoDL hemolysis and ESMFold confidence models. Of 16 synthesised peptides tested against a 37-strain panel, three (AMP2, AMP7, AMP9) completely inhibited at least one strain, a hit rate of 18.75%. The hit rate is low and activity is narrow.
ai_technology: Surrogate-guided self-play Monte Carlo tree search (reinforcement learning)
organization: Taipei Tzu Chi Hospital; National Central University

evidence.tested: In vitro agar dilution MIC assays of 16 synthesised peptides against 37 strains.
evidence.unknown: Low hit rate and narrow strain activity; no baseline comparison seen in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement learning search over peptide sequences guided by surrogate models.
